description.hook: Sulayman stood dead against his staff and the jinn under his command kept working. They only found out when a creature of the earth ate through it.
description.body:
That is Qur'an 34:14, in Surah Saba'. The detail the verse stops to make is not the death, it is the ignorance: the jinn were standing in front of a dead king and could not tell. The verse says it plainly -- had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in that humiliating labour.

This video takes that verse where it actually leads. If jinn could not perceive a death happening in front of them, the claim that a jinn is the reason a soothsayer knows your future, your marriage or your dead relative does not survive its own source text. The Qur'an closes the door from the inside.

What the video covers:
- the scene in Saba' 34:14 and why the staff detail is the point
- what 'al-ghayb' means and who the Qur'an restricts it to
- why 'the jinn told me' fails on the Qur'an's own terms
- what the jinn in Surah al-Jinn admit about their own limits

If this was useful, the fastest way to help is to send it to the one person you know who has been to a fortune teller.

pinned_comment:
The verse is Saba' 34:14. The part almost nobody quotes is the reason it is there at all: the jinn were beside a dead king and could not tell he had died. The Qur'an then says it outright -- had they known the unseen, they would never have stayed in that labour.

So the honest question for anyone who has been to a fortune teller, or knows someone who has: what were you actually told, and did it happen the way it was told to you? I read every reply.

Sulayman had already died. The jinn kept working. They found out when a creature of the earth ate through his staff.

New video is up -- the verse is 34:14, and it does more damage to fortune telling than any argument from outside the text. Watch it and tell me if you have heard this one before.
